beats.narration_text: This is Liam, in for Sanjana. A short briefing for Humanitarians AI fellows — how the video review process works, end to end.

props.command: claude "walk me through the Humanitarians AI YouTube video review process — for a new fellow."
props.runningText: this is Liam, in for Sanjana…

beats.role_note: one breath, non-technical — what this is and why care
beats.narration_text: Every week a fellow ships two videos, each in landscape and vertical — four files total. Sanjana or Pooja review against six criteria, the approved videos land in a Queue playlist, and Prof. Brown and Prof. Nina give the final call before anything publishes. This video is the map of that pipeline.
beats.visual_intent: Title card: 'HAI FELLOWS · VIDEO REVIEW PROCESS' — under it a three-stop pipeline: 'Fellow → PM review → Queue → Prof. Brown & Prof. Nina'. No composer.

beats.narration_text: The week is two videos, four files. Video one — a STEM or AI topic the fellow is interested in. Video two — a progress update on the fellow's assigned project. Each video ships in both 16 by 9 and 9 by 16. A fellow can swap a topic for a passion project, as long as at least one of the four videos across any two-week window is a real research or project update. The update is the floor, not the ceiling.
beats.visual_intent: Grid: two rows (Video 1, Video 2), two columns (16:9, 9:16). Under it: 'at least 1 research update per rolling two-week window'.

beats.narration_text: The path is five steps. One — the fellow uploads to the shared Google Drive folder and notifies Sanjana or Pooja. Two — Sanjana or Pooja review against the criteria. Three — quality checks: format, resolution, content. Four — approved videos go to the Humanitarians AI YouTube channel, into the Queue playlist. Five — Prof. Brown and Prof. Nina give the final feedback. Publish, or send back. Only the first two steps are the fellow's — the rest is the pipeline doing its work.
beats.visual_intent: Vertical numbered list, 5 steps, each with its owner tag on the right: Fellow → Sanjana/Pooja → Sanjana/Pooja → HAI channel/Queue → Prof. Brown & Prof. Nina.

beats.role_note: the non-negotiables of the artifact itself
beats.narration_text: The artifact has hard rules. Every video is built in Brutalist, and the version has to be the current week's — not last week's cache. Resolution is 4K at the source, and it has to still be 4K after YouTube's transcode; a 4K master that streams at 1080p failed. Both aspect ratios are required — not one, not a crop of the other. And every video opens with the same line: hi, I am your name, and this video is about the summary of the topic. That intro is not a suggestion.
beats.visual_intent: Four labeled tiles: 'Brutalist (latest weekly)', '4K (3840x2160)', '16:9 + 9:16', 'Intro line'. The intro tile prints the exact template underneath.

beats.narration_text: The PM approval gate is six checks, in order. Brutalist format followed correctly. 4K at source, 4K after upload. Both 16 by 9 and 9 by 16 delivered. Formatting clean — images render, text legible on desktop and mobile. The intro line is present in the required form. And the viewer walks away with a real takeaway — one thing they can now do, or know, that they could not before. All six clear — then it moves to the Queue.

props.title: pm_review_checklist.md
props.code:
# PM Approval - six criteria, all six must pass

1. Brutalist format followed correctly
2. 4K at source AND 4K after YouTube upload
3. Both 16:9 and 9:16 versions delivered
4. Formatting clean - images render, text legible
   on desktop and mobile
5. Intro line present:
   "Hi, I am [Your Name], and this video is
   about [summary of topic]."
6. Viewer gains a real takeaway from the video

# All six pass -> upload to HAI YouTube, Queue playlist
# Prof. Brown & Prof. Nina review after upload

beats.role_note: how files enter the shared folder
beats.narration_text: Naming is enforced at upload. Every file — both aspect ratios of both weekly videos — gets the same base: project name, underscore, volunteer name. No spaces, no dates, no v2, no final. Version history lives in GitHub, not in filenames. The files go into the shared Drive folder; then the fellow pings Sanjana or Pooja that the upload is ready.
beats.visual_intent: Filename recipe card: 'ProjectName_VolunteerName' — red X's next to 'ProjectName VolunteerName' and 'ProjectName_VolunteerName_v2'. Below: shared-Drive icon + 'notify Sanjana or Pooja'.

beats.role_note: two rules that finish the submission
beats.narration_text: Two closing rules. First, GitHub is mandatory — the code or source project used to make the film is uploaded, and the repository URL is shared with the video files at submission time. No repo, no upload. Second, the Shorts side of the channel: 9 by 16 posts are scheduled at least one hour after the previous Short, channel-wide, and each Short links to the most popular existing Humanitarians AI video on a related subject. That link is picked at scheduling time, not from memory.
beats.visual_intent: Two panels. Left: GitHub mark + 'repo URL required with every submission'. Right: two clock dials 60 min apart + 'link to most popular related HAI video'.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — what the fellow does after watching
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Before your next submission — check your Brutalist version, render at 4K, produce both aspects natively, and open with the intro line as written. Rename the files, push the code to GitHub, drop the URL alongside the videos, and tell Sanjana or Pooja the folder is ready. If you do not have a PM yet, that message comes straight to Sanjana. That is the whole pipeline.
